title: Billing Adjustments Training Q&A: Late Payment Charges Refunded with a Meter Error on Electric Service by Rate Schedule
content:
The questions below are answered by the Electric Service by Rate Schedule rule on late payment charges that were charged while a meter was running fast.

**Which late payment charges are concerned?** The late payment charges on the service account dated in the rebill window of the meter error correction. The latest late payment charge on the account is left out when it is dated after the test was performed (the latest test found fast).

**When are they refunded in full?** When such late payment charges exist and the account carries a disconnect date for nonpayment.

**When are they refunded in part?** When such late payment charges exist and the account carries no disconnect date: they are refunded at the overbilled share of the meter error, the late payment charges multiplied by that share and rounded to the cent.

**And otherwise?** When no such late payment charge exists, no late payment charge is refunded.

**Where does the late charge refund go?** It is added to the meter error refund on the same credit.

### Decision table

| Late payment charges in the window, after leaving out a latest charge dated after the test | Disconnect date on the account | Late charge refund |
|---|---|---|
| Above zero | Present | Those charges in full |
| Above zero | None | Those charges multiplied by the overbilled share, rounded to the cent |
| Zero | Any | Nothing |

### Hypothetical worked case

The window holds three late payment charges of $3.00, $3.00 and $4.12, and the $4.12 charge is the latest on the account and is dated after the fast test was performed. The charges counted are $6.00.

- With a disconnect date on the account, the late charge refund is $6.00.
- With no disconnect date and an overbilled share of 4 divided by 104, the refund is $6.00 multiplied by 4 and divided by 104, $0.2308, which rounds to $0.23.
